gen-dafont-hammerhead-author: Heavy tubing up top, then a gentler voice below: Hammerhead keeps one thick, unmodulated line through every bend, while Author's text serif adds a slight swell and finer crossbars. Body text around 16px suits it.
gen-dafont-helsinki-fs-bespoke-slab: Wide, marker-plain letters lead the way. Helsinki stretches sideways with a ballpoint's pressureless line, while Bespoke Slab stands taller in every lowercase letter and gives the page a grounded, classic serif footing.
gen-dafont-hero-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab reads as a dignified serif whose lowercase sits very close to the height of its capitals, a tight, tidy line beneath Hero's widely spaced sweep. Paragraphs would move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-horizon-archivo: Glowing neon-glass tubes, nearly sealed shut at every round. Archivo takes over below with curves that open outward and a commanding x-height, so the closed heading letters give way to a body that breathes.
gen-dafont-impact-label-fs-gambetta: Impact Label stands each letter apart like beads on a rod, with a high-set x-height and c-ends pointing away from each other like pincers. Gambetta's text serif then carries a longer read gracefully, its stroke weight shifting noticeably but never dramatically.
gen-dafont-impact-label-fs-hind: Hind keeps its lowercase close to capital height. Under Impact Label's bead-like letters, its strokes hold the steadiness of a drawn string, so a body size a notch above default would let those open c-ends show.
gen-dafont-impact-label-fs-nunito: Nunito brings big round lowercase bowls, with terminals that finish well clear of the stem. Beneath Impact Label's heavy, pincer-ended letters, Nunito supplies the friendliness, and that softness is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-impact-label-fs-roundo: Commanding up top, mild below. Impact Label towers on its high x-height, while Roundo's sans strokes look drawn with a fixed pen, so a long passage moves along with small counters that never clog.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-atkinson-hype: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next has lowercase eyes as big as washers, with rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook. Against Impact Label's heavy, bead-like letters, its open, approachable build is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-open-sans: Open Sans reads smoothly, with no clogged curves and bulky lowercase proportions. Under Impact Label's heavy, pincer-ended heading, a longer passage would feel modern and easy to move through without any snagging.
